# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestures 👍 - a thumbs up, which reads as simple affirmation/confirmation. This likely confirms my last guess: that the count of five ☝ meant "wire 5" (red).

This is a clean, unambiguous positive signal. I should relay this confirmation to Blind so they know which wire is being indicated, while still being cautious - a single thumbs up confirms my interpretation but I don't have confirmation of what action to take (cut it? don't cut it? something else?). I should ask Mute for the action too, and give Blind the wire identity now.

```
speak(text="Blind, Mute confirmed with thumbs up that the number five points to wire 5, which is red on my board. That's the target wire. Mute, please now signal what to do with wire 5 - cut it, leave it, or something else. Blind, still hold action until we know what to do with it.")
wait()
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute gestures ✌ (two fingers/victory sign) - a single symbol this time, distinct from the count-of-one-finger-five-times pattern. This could mean:
- The number 2 (a new instruction/step number)
- A binary choice - "option 2" (e.g., of two possible actions: cut or don't cut)
- Could relate back to earlier context where ✌ appeared paired with ☝ (possibly "2 and 1" meant something like wire 2, or step 2)

Given the flow: we identified wire 5 (red) as the target. Now Mute sends ✌ alone. This could be answering "what to do" with an encoded action number - e.g. action 2 = "cut", action 1 = "leave", or similar simple manual encoding.

I don't have enough certainty to declare an action to Blind. I should ask Mute to clarify what ✌ means in this context - is it an action code, or something else - while telling Blind to keep holding.

```
speak(text="Mute, I saw a single two-finger sign, separate from the five-count. If this is an action code, please clarify: does two mean cut the wire, or does it mean something else like leave it, or refer to a different step? Blind, continue to hold, no action yet on wire 5.")
wait()
```

TURN 14
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

Mute now sends ✊ (fist) alone. This is yet another single symbol, distinct from ✌ and from the five-☝ count. Let me think about what pattern might be forming.

Possible encoding: Mute might be trying to spell out or signal a sequence of numbers one at a time now, since gestures are limited and speech isn't available to Mute. Recall earlier context (from turn 11, referencing older turns): "✊,☝" and "✌,☝" were seen as pairs before. Now sequence is: ☝×5, then 👍, then ✌ alone, then ✊ alone.

Maybe Mute is counting through digits one at a time across turns, since only one gesture fits per turn easily, or deliberately spacing them to avoid ambiguity. Sequence so far after the "wire 5 confirmed" moment: ✌, ✊. If these are digits: ✌=2, ✊=0 (fist could represent "0" - a closed hand, no fingers up). That would give "20" or sequentially "2" then "0".

Alternatively ✊ might mean "no"/"stop"/"zero" contrasted with 👍 "yes". If ✌ was "cut" is wrong guess and ✊ now means "no, don't cut" - contradicting my two hypotheses.

Given genuine ambiguity, I must not let Blind act without clarity. I will report the raw new symbol, keep prior context, and ask Mute to slow down / clarify meaning explicitly using consistent yes/no vocabulary (👍/✊ or 👍/👎).

```
speak(text="Mute, I now see a closed fist alone, after the two-finger sign before it. I am not sure if fist means zero, no, or stop. Please use thumbs up for yes and thumbs down for no from now on, to avoid confusion. Blind, keep holding, no action on wire 5 yet.")
wait()
```
